contact_oxidation: A four-wire survey places 1.8 V of the loss across the removable feed contact and less than 0.03 V along the wire. The surveyed mating faces carry a layer whose surface spectrum and depth profile identify oxidized metal above the clean substrate; the clean-metal control lacks that layer, and nonmetallic contaminant residues are below the stated detection bound. Contact force meets specification. Cleaning those faces restores a 23.9 V load terminal without changing the regulator. Its unloaded and loaded setpoints and the measured reservoir capacitance remain within limits.
regulator_drift: The output measures 21.6 V both at the regulator pins and at the dummy load; intervening contacts and wire lose less than 0.03 V. A calibrated meter on the internal reference shows its target has shifted while the input stays at 24.0 V. A reference-module substitution restores the output. Contacts are clean, flex continuity is stable, and reservoir capacitance and series resistance meet limits. The same surface assay matches the clean-metal control at the low-loss contact faces.
harness_conductor_fracture: At one bend angle an internal conductor gap opens for 20 ms while both end contacts remain closed and the upstream source is live. The board input is absent for that measured interval and output crosses its restart threshold. Imaging that cable section shows separated strands beneath intact insulation. A temporary parallel lead removes the added interruption and restart at the same angle. With the original reservoir fitted, a separate deliberate 7 ms input gap is bridged normally, including the documented 2 ms source interruptions; a matched 20 ms gap reproduces the threshold crossing predicted by its nominal measured capacitance and series resistance.
supply_capacitor_degradation: Cable continuity stays below 0.1 ohm through the entire motion, including the angle that previously caused a reboot. Each normal 2 ms supply interruption is followed by a steep output decay. The removed reservoir measures one fifth of its rated capacitance and elevated series resistance. Substituting that component restores hold-up; neither a parallel cable nor a different contact position changes the trace.
connector_fatigue: Each isolated and paired memory write retains both original payloads and ready bits, and decoded injection drains after release. On electrical input a permanently thinned mating spring has inadequate measured force even at full rated seating. Its contact opens during normal movement before the decoder receives a frame, while the feed wires remain continuous. A mechanically supported contact passes the same physical stream without changing any memory address; changing the address pair alone leaves the measured contact openings.
interface_buffer_fault: The seated contacts maintain specified force and uninterrupted physical input. Both frames decode correctly, but two supported queue addresses that differ in one address bit select the same internal storage cell: writing the second frame clears the first entry's ready state. Each address alone retains data, and other address pairs coexist normally. Readback and internal select-line capture locate that alias inside interface queue memory. Allocating the two entries to a nonaliasing pair restores dequeue under the same valid physical stream, with free capacity and unchanged connector movement.
clock_recovery_instability: Both line lengths have specified end admittance and independently verified usable physical input without the abnormal reflection. The internal receive-loop phase response becomes unbounded at supported modulation frequencies despite that input; an independent receiver tracks it normally. Queue progress remains normal after independent decoding. The instability does not shift with propagation length.
termination_impedance_error: The measured end admittance is incorrect and a distorted reflected edge moves in time exactly with changed line length. A valid independent physical input preserves receiver phase lock. The failing waveform is already distorted before recovery, and the queue handles independently decoded frames. The length transformation localizes the fault to the fixed line end.
surface_deposit: A removable film covers the optical window, and transmission through that isolated window is reduced. Cleaning the window restores both optical standards on both readouts. With the input dark, the electrical baseline agrees with specification before and after cleaning; an injected electrical span also matches its reference. Digitizer intervals remain uniform. No internal calibration adjustment is needed.
reference_offset: The clean window transmits normally and further cleaning changes neither standard. With a sealed dark input, the probe's internal reference node sits 0.18 V above its specified zero on both readouts. Two standards retain the correct separation but share that same displacement. Replacing the reference module restores zero; excitation, injected span and sample intervals remain unchanged.
sampling_clock_jitter: The continuous conditioned vector has the specified radius and follows the independently measured stage angle for both stimuli. Each digitized sine/cosine pair still lies on that circle, but its angular position disagrees with the angle expected at a uniform sample time. Independent aperture timestamps show irregular actual intervals and align every pair with the corresponding analog angle at its true capture time. Driving the same acquisition from the regular external aperture source removes the angular-time error without changing radius, conditioner or excitation.
transducer_gain_error: For both the angle stage and electrical simulator, the continuous conditioned sine/cosine vector has the correct angular progression but a uniformly reduced radius across the full circle, with both zero levels correct. The same fixed proportional deficit is present during static angle holds and localized across the assembly's common conditioning stage; its measured input vector has the specified radius. The digitizer follows that already reduced analog vector with regular actual apertures. A timing substitution leaves the static and rotating radius deficit unchanged.
belt_slip: The drive pulley advances relative to painted marks on the V-belt under load, and phase is already lost at the belt-driven shaft. Gear input-to-output ratio remains consistent through each tooth sector; measured tooth profiles meet wear limits. Restoring belt tension to specification removes the relative motion and travel deficit without changing the gears or guide.
gear_wear: Belt marks and both pulley encoders stay phase-aligned at the fault load. The lost travel first appears across the gear stage and repeats at the same tooth sector. Profilometry shows rounded, thinned engagement surfaces there rather than a fresh fracture. A matched gear removes the sector-dependent loss with the original belt; guide force and hub marks remain unchanged.
guide_binding: With the drive disconnected, pull force rises from 8 N to 70 N at the same slide position in both directions. Inspection finds a guide liner swollen into the running clearance. Shaft and hub move together on reversal. Replacing the liner restores an approximately flat force map and continuous travel with the original drive and coupling retained.
coupler_looseness: The disconnected slide traverses at 8 to 10 N across its stroke and its guide clearance is within limits. On reversal, the shaft turns 6 degrees before the hub follows; witness marks separate at the clamp. Clamp engagement is below specification. Correctly seating and tightening that clamp removes the angular delay while the guide, belt and gear stages remain fitted.

disclosure_contract.scope: Declared fine mechanism only; initial routing, not final root-cause repair
disclosure_contract.unavailable_response_policy: generic status only; raw error bodies, latency and credentials are not released

check_contract.scope: simulated diagnostic channels; not claims about field diagnostics

public_request: Choose the initial service route for a device that cannot complete its normal cycle.

mechanism_definitions.contact_oxidation: An electrically resistive oxide or tarnish film on a supply contact, supported by localized contact and surface evidence. A loose clean contact or broken internal conductor is different.
mechanism_definitions.regulator_drift: The internal regulated voltage moves away from its setpoint with a stable incoming supply.
mechanism_definitions.harness_conductor_fracture: A broken supply conductor interrupts continuity, including under flexing.
mechanism_definitions.supply_capacitor_degradation: Reduced charge storage or excessive series resistance causes rail sag or ripple.
mechanism_definitions.connector_fatigue: Permanent wear or fatigue of a communication mating contact produces inadequate contact force or intermittent opening. A merely unseated intact connector, feed-wire fracture, or queue stall is different.
mechanism_definitions.interface_buffer_fault: A communication interface queue stalls despite a working physical signal path.
mechanism_definitions.termination_impedance_error: Incorrect line termination causes reflections or signal distortion.
mechanism_definitions.clock_recovery_instability: Receive timing loses phase lock despite a usable physical input signal.
mechanism_definitions.surface_deposit: Material on the sensing surface changes its measurement response.
mechanism_definitions.reference_offset: An additive baseline defect localized to the sensor assembly internal zero/reference path. A mis-set external reference fixture or excitation source is outside this mechanism.
mechanism_definitions.transducer_gain_error: An intrinsic proportional span defect localized to the transducer assembly, including its conditioning module, under correct excitation and independent stimuli. Optical surface attenuation, wrong external calibration, and baseline displacement are different.
mechanism_definitions.sampling_clock_jitter: Irregular acquisition timing inside the measurement channel distorts a changing signal despite a correct analog response; a moving stimulus alone is not sufficient.
mechanism_definitions.belt_slip: A frictional drive belt moves relative to its pulley under load. Gear engagement loss, guide resistance and shaft-to-hub clearance are separate boundaries.
mechanism_definitions.gear_wear: Worn gear engagement surfaces fail to transmit commanded motion.
mechanism_definitions.guide_binding: A mechanical guide obstructs otherwise correctly driven travel.
mechanism_definitions.coupler_looseness: A loose shaft coupling or hub absorbs motion before transferring it.

causal_scope: Primary defect at the declared diagnostic boundary, not all upstream causes. Different plausible leaves or independent concurrent causes must remain unresolved when observations do not distinguish them.
